entities.name: Adaptation
entities.definition: A heritable characteristic, structure, behaviour, or physiological trait that enhances an organism's ability to survive and reproduce in its environment, having arisen through natural selection acting on genetic variation over generations.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences / UNESCO Biology Framework

entities.name: Allele
entities.definition: One of the alternative forms of a gene that occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes and can specify alternative versions of a trait; a diploid organism carries two alleles for each autosomal gene, which may be identical (homozygous) or different (heterozygous).

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Animal Cell
entities.definition: A eukaryotic cell characteristic of animals, enclosed by a flexible plasma membrane, lacking a cell wall and chloroplasts, and containing membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, lysosomes, and a nucleus.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Cell
entities.definition: The basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all known living organisms. Cells carry out essential life processes, contain hereditary material, and arise from pre-existing cells.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences / UNESCO Biology Framework

entities.name: Cellular Respiration
entities.definition: The metabolic process by which cells break down organic molecules (such as glucose) to release energy stored in ATP molecules, utilizing oxygen in aerobic respiration and producing carbon dioxide and water.

provenance.source: International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

entities.name: Chromosome
entities.definition: A long, linear (or circular in prokaryotes) structure of DNA tightly coiled around histone and other proteins, carrying many genes and serving as the unit of genetic organization that is replicated and partitioned during cell division.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)
entities.definition: A double-stranded helical nucleic acid molecule storing genetic instructions used in the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.

provenance.source: IUPAC-IUBMB Joint Commission on Biochemical Nomenclature

entities.name: DNA Replication
entities.definition: The semi-conservative process by which a cell copies its double-stranded DNA before division, in which each parental strand serves as a template for the synthesis of a complementary new strand through the coordinated action of enzymes at an unwound replication fork.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Ecosystem
entities.definition: A biological community of interacting organisms (biotic factors) together with their non-living physical and chemical environment (abiotic factors), functioning as an integrated ecological system.

provenance.source: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) / UNESCO

entities.name: Energy Flow in Ecosystems
entities.definition: The one-way, non-cyclical movement of energy through an ecosystem, entering as sunlight captured by producers, passing through successive trophic levels as chemical energy, and being progressively lost to the environment as heat through respiration at each transfer.

provenance.source: Raymond Lindeman; Fundamentals of Ecology (Odum)

entities.name: Enzyme
entities.definition: A biological catalyst (typically a protein) that speeds up specific biochemical reactions by lowering activation energy without being consumed in the reaction.

provenance.source: International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

entities.name: Food Chain
entities.definition: A linear sequence of organisms within an ecosystem along which energy and nutrients are transferred as one organism is consumed by the next, beginning typically with a producer and passing through consumers of successive trophic levels.

provenance.source: United States National Science Foundation, Ecology Education

entities.name: Gene
entities.definition: The basic physical and functional unit of heredity, composed of a specific sequence of nucleotides along a DNA molecule that codes for a specific functional polypeptide (protein) or RNA product.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Glycolysis
entities.definition: The first stage of cellular respiration, a ten-step cytosolic pathway that breaks down one molecule of glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, producing a net yield of two ATP and two NADH without requiring oxygen, and providing substrates for further aerobic or anaerobic reactions.

provenance.source: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry

entities.name: Homeostasis
entities.definition: The maintenance of a stable internal environment (temperature, pH, water and solute balance, glucose levels) within living organisms despite changes in the external environment, achieved through regulatory feedback mechanisms.

provenance.source: International Union of Physiological Sciences

entities.name: Hormone
entities.definition: A chemical messenger secreted by endocrine glands or specialized cells into the bloodstream or extracellular fluid that travels to target cells expressing specific receptors, where it triggers physiological responses, helping to regulate metabolism, growth, reproduction, and homeostasis.

provenance.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology

entities.name: Immune System
entities.definition: The coordinated network of organs, cells, and molecules that defends the body against pathogens and other foreign substances, comprising nonspecific (innate) mechanisms such as barriers and phagocytes and specific (adaptive) responses including antibody production and immunological memory.

provenance.source: World Health Organization; International Union of Physiological Sciences

entities.name: Inheritance Patterns
entities.definition: The recurring ways in which traits and alleles are transmitted from parents to offspring, including Mendelian patterns (dominant, recessive, codominant, and incomplete dominance) and non-Mendelian patterns such as sex linkage, multiple alleles, polygenic inheritance, and pleiotropy.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Meiosis
entities.definition: A specialized two-stage cell division (meiosis I and meiosis II) in diploid organisms that produces four genetically distinct haploid gametes or spores, halving the chromosome number and generating genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Mitosis
entities.definition: The stage of the cell cycle in which a eukaryotic cell's nucleus divides, its duplicated chromosomes separating into two genetically identical daughter nuclei, so that each daughter cell receives the same diploid chromosome complement as the parent.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Mutation
entities.definition: A heritable change in the nucleotide sequence of a genome, arising from errors in DNA replication, repair, or recombination, or from environmental mutagens; mutations range from single base changes (point mutations) to large chromosomal rearrangements.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Natural Selection
entities.definition: The evolutionary process by which organisms possessing heritable traits better suited to their environment tend to survive and reproduce at higher rates, passing advantageous alleles to subsequent generations.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences / UNESCO Biology Framework

entities.name: Nervous System
entities.definition: The organ system that enables rapid sensing, integration, and response to internal and external stimuli through electrical and chemical signalling, comprising the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system of nerves connecting them to the body.

provenance.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology

entities.name: Neuron
entities.definition: The electrically excitable nerve cell that is the fundamental signalling unit of the nervous system, composed of dendrites receiving signals, a cell body integrating them, and an axon conducting action potentials that release neurotransmitters at synapses to transmit information to other cells.

provenance.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology

entities.name: Nucleus
entities.definition: The membrane-bound organelle in eukaryotic cells that contains most of the cell's genetic material (DNA) and directs cell activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Osmosis
entities.definition: The net movement of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration (higher water concentration) to a region of higher solute concentration (lower water concentration), equalizing concentration by water flow.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Photosynthesis
entities.definition: The biological process by which autotrophic organisms (such as plants and algae) convert light energy into stored chemical energy in glucose, using carbon dioxide and water while releasing oxygen as a byproduct.

provenance.source: UNESCO Science Education Framework / IUPAC

entities.name: Plant Cell
entities.definition: A eukaryotic cell characteristic of plants, distinguished by a rigid cellulose cell wall, a large central vacuole for turgor pressure, and plastids such as chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

provenance.source: International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Population Dynamics
entities.definition: The study of how population size, density, age structure, and distribution change over time and space in response to birth, death, immigration, and emigration, modulated by resource availability, competition, predation, and other density-dependent and density-independent factors.

provenance.source: Ecology (Odum); International Union of Biological Sciences

entities.name: Protein Synthesis
entities.definition: The two-stage gene-expression pathway by which the information in a gene's DNA is converted into a functional polypeptide: transcription produces messenger RNA from a DNA template, and translation assembles amino acids into a protein on ribosomes.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Speciation
entities.definition: The evolutionary process by which populations diverge genetically to the point that they become reproductively isolated from one another, forming distinct species; it commonly proceeds through allopatric (geographic separation) or sympatric (within a shared range) mechanisms.

provenance.source: The Origin of Species (Charles Darwin); Campbell Biology

entities.name: Transcription
entities.definition: The first stage of gene expression, in which the enzyme RNA polymerase uses one strand of a DNA template (the template strand) to synthesize a complementary single-stranded RNA molecule, producing messenger RNA, transfer RNA, or ribosomal RNA from a specific gene.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Translation
entities.definition: The process in which the nucleotide sequence of messenger RNA is decoded by ribosomes to assemble a polypeptide chain, with transfer RNA molecules matching successive codons to their corresponding amino acids and linking them into proteins.

provenance.source: Campbell Biology

entities.name: Acid
entities.definition: A chemical substance that releases hydrogen ions (H⁺ or hydronium H₃O⁺) in aqueous solution, tastes sour, turns blue litmus paper red, has a pH less than 7, and reacts with bases to form salts and water.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Activation Energy
entities.definition: The minimum energy that colliding reactant particles must possess for a reaction to occur, forming an activated complex. Activation energy governs the rate of a reaction through the exponential Arrhenius relationship with temperature.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Alcohol
entities.definition: An organic compound containing one or more hydroxyl (—OH) functional groups bonded to a saturated carbon atom. Alcohols are polar, hydrogen-bonding liquids that range from methanol and ethanol to high-molecular-mass polyols.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Alkane
entities.definition: A saturated hydrocarbon in which every carbon atom is bonded to others by single covalent bonds only, with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for acyclic alkanes. Alkanes are the simplest homologous series of organic compounds.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Alkene
entities.definition: An unsaturated hydrocarbon that contains at least one carbon-to-carbon double bond, with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ as a member of the homologous series. The presence of the double bond makes alkenes more reactive than alkanes.
entities.equation: C_n H_{2n}  (acyclic alkenes with one double bond, n ≥ 2)

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Atom
entities.definition: The smallest unit of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element. An atom consists of a dense central nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by a cloud of electrons.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Base
entities.definition: A chemical substance that reacts with acids to form salt and water, accepts protons (H⁺), or releases hydroxide ions (OH⁻) in aqueous solution (alkali). Bases taste bitter, feel slippery, turn red litmus paper blue, and have a pH greater than 7.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Carboxylic Acid
entities.definition: An organic compound containing a carboxyl functional group (—COOH), a carbonyl group bonded to a hydroxyl group. Carboxylic acids are weak acids that donate a proton from the hydroxyl group to form carboxylate anions.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Catalyst
entities.definition: A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway of lower activation energy, while itself being regenerated and not consumed overall. A catalyst does not alter the equilibrium position or product yield.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Balanced Chemical Equation
entities.definition: A symbolic representation of a chemical reaction showing reactants on the left and products on the right, with coefficient ratios balanced so that the number of atoms of each element is conserved across the arrow.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Chemical Equilibrium
entities.definition: The state of a reversible reaction in which the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time. Equilibrium is dynamic and does not imply equal quantities of reactants and products.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Chemical Reaction
entities.definition: A process in which one or more substances (reactants) are chemically transformed into one or more different substances (products) through the breaking and forming of chemical bonds, conserving total mass and atoms.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Combustion
entities.definition: A rapid chemical reaction between a substance and an oxidant (usually oxygen) that releases heat and light. Complete combustion of hydrocarbons produces carbon dioxide and water; incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and soot.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Chemical Compound
entities.definition: A pure substance formed when two or more different chemical elements are chemically bonded together in a fixed stoichiometric ratio. Compounds have chemical properties distinct from their constituent elements.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Covalent Bond
entities.definition: A chemical bond formed when two non-metal atoms share one or more pairs of valence electrons, achieving stable noble-gas electron configurations through mutual electrostatic attraction between shared electrons and nuclei.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Diffusion
entities.definition: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, driven by the random thermal motion of particles, until concentrations equalize.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Electrochemical Cell
entities.definition: A device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy or, conversely, uses electrical energy to drive a chemical reaction. Galvanic (voltaic) cells generate electricity from spontaneous redox reactions, while electrolytic cells use an external voltage.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Electrolysis
entities.definition: The decomposition of a compound into its elements or simpler substances by passing an electric current through an electrolyte. Electrolysis is driven by an external voltage and is the key process in an electrolytic cell, enabling nonspontaneous redox reactions.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Electron
entities.definition: A stable subatomic particle carrying a negative elementary electric charge (-1e) and a mass approximately 1/1836th of a proton (9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg), occupying atomic orbitals surrounding the nucleus.

provenance.source: IUPAC Gold Book

entities.name: Chemical Element
entities.definition: A pure chemical substance consisting of atoms that all have the same number of protons in their atomic nuclei. Elements cannot be broken down into simpler substances by ordinary chemical reactions.

provenance.source: IUPAC Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry

entities.name: Enthalpy
entities.definition: A thermodynamic quantity equal to the internal energy of a system plus the product of its pressure and volume, H = U + PV. The change in enthalpy, ΔH, measures the heat absorbed or released by a process at constant pressure.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Entropy
entities.definition: A thermodynamic quantity that measures the dispersal of energy or the number of microscopic arrangements (microstates) available to a system, expressed as a measure of disorder. The entropy of an isolated system tends to increase in spontaneous processes.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Equilibrium Constant
entities.definition: A dimensionless quantity that characterizes the position of a chemical equilibrium. For a reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD it is the ratio of product concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients to reactant concentrations raised to theirs, at a given temperature.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Functional Group
entities.definition: A specific atom or group of atoms within an organic molecule that determines the characteristic chemical reactions and properties of that molecule. The same functional group confers predictable behaviour regardless of the carbon skeleton to which it is attached.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Gibbs Free Energy
entities.definition: A thermodynamic quantity, G = H − TS, that combines enthalpy and entropy to predict whether a process is spontaneous at constant temperature and pressure. A negative Gibbs free energy change indicates a spontaneous process.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Hydrocarbon
entities.definition: An organic molecule composed entirely of carbon and hydrogen atoms. Hydrocarbons are the fundamental framework of organic chemistry, classified into alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compounds according to the bonding between carbon atoms.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Ionic Bond
entities.definition: A chemical bond formed through the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions, resulting from the complete transfer of one or more valence electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Isomer
entities.definition: One of two or more compounds that have the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms, and therefore different structures or spatial configurations. Isomerism may be structural (constitutional) or stereochemical.

provenance.source: Clayden Organic Chemistry

entities.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
entities.definition: The principle stating that if a dynamic equilibrium is disturbed by changing a condition such as concentration, pressure, or temperature, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that tends to counteract that change and re-establish equilibrium.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Matter
entities.definition: Anything that has mass and takes up space by occupying volume. Matter is composed of fundamental particles and exists in various physical states depending on thermal energy and pressure.

provenance.source: IUPAC Gold Book / UNESCO Science Education Framework

entities.name: Mixture
entities.definition: A physical combination of two or more substances that are not chemically bonded, can vary in composition, and can be separated by physical means. Homogeneous mixtures are uniform throughout; heterogeneous mixtures are not.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Neutralization Reaction
entities.definition: A chemical reaction between an acid and a base (or alkali) producing a salt and water, in which hydrogen ions (H⁺) from the acid react with hydroxide ions (OH⁻) from the base to form neutral water molecules (H₂O).

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Oxidation Number
entities.definition: A bookkeeping number assigned to an atom in a compound or ion that represents the charge the atom would have if all bonds to atoms of different electronegativity were ionic. Oxidation numbers track electron transfer in oxidation-reduction reactions.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Oxidation-Reduction
entities.definition: A class of chemical reactions involving the transfer of electrons between species, in which oxidation is the loss of electrons and reduction is the gain of electrons. Oxidation and reduction always occur together, with one species being oxidized and another reduced.
entities.equation: X → Xⁿ⁺ + ne⁻  (oxidation);  Y + ne⁻ → Yⁿ⁻  (reduction)

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Periodic Table of Elements
entities.definition: A tabular arrangement of chemical elements ordered by increasing atomic number, displaying recurring (periodic) trends in chemical and physical properties across periods (rows) and groups (columns).

provenance.source: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements

entities.name: pH Scale
entities.definition: A logarithmic scale measuring the acidity or alkalinity of an aqueous solution, defined as the negative base-10 logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration (pH = -log₁₀[H⁺]), ranging from 0 (highly acidic) to 14 (highly alkaline), with 7 being neutral.

provenance.source: IUPAC Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Polymer
entities.definition: A large molecule built from many repeating monomer units joined by covalent bonds. Polymers may be natural, such as proteins and cellulose, or synthetic, such as polyethylene and nylon, formed by addition or condensation polymerization.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Proton
entities.definition: A stable subatomic particle occurring in all atomic nuclei, carrying a positive elementary electric charge (+1e) and a mass of approximately 1 atomic mass unit (1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg).

provenance.source: IUPAC Gold Book

entities.name: Reaction Rate
entities.definition: The change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time during a chemical reaction, usually expressed as the decrease in reactant concentration or increase in product concentration per second. Reaction rates depend on concentration, temperature, and the presence of a catalyst.

provenance.source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Salt
entities.definition: An ionic compound formed when the hydrogen ion of an acid is replaced by a metal ion (or ammonium ion), typically produced by neutralization of an acid with a base. Common table salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

provenance.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology

entities.name: Earth Atmosphere
entities.definition: The layer of gases surrounding Earth, retained by Earth's gravity, composed primarily of nitrogen (78%) and oxygen (21%), which absorbs ultraviolet radiation, warms the surface via the greenhouse effect, and regulates weather.

provenance.source: NOAA / WMO Atmospheric Science Standards

entities.name: Big Bang Theory
entities.definition: The prevailing cosmological model describing the early development and metric expansion of the universe from an extremely hot, dense state approximately 13.8 billion years ago.

provenance.source: International Astronomical Union (IAU) / NASA Cosmology Framework

entities.name: Earth System
entities.definition: The integrated complex of physical, chemical, biological, and geological processes interacting across Earth's four major interconnected spheres: the geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere.

provenance.source: NASA Earth System Science Framework / AGU

entities.name: Greenhouse Effect
entities.definition: The process by which greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere (such as water vapor, CO₂, CH₄) absorb outgoing infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface and re-radiate thermal energy in all directions, warming the lower atmosphere.

provenance.source: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report / WMO

entities.name: Plate Tectonics
entities.definition: The unifying geological theory explaining that Earth's rigid outer shell (lithosphere) is divided into several large plates that move slowly over the asthenosphere, driven by mantle convection currents.

provenance.source: USGS / AGU Earth Science Education Framework

entities.name: Rock Cycle
entities.definition: The continuous transformation of the three rock families — igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic — through weathering, erosion, deposition, burial, heat, pressure, and melting, driven by Earth's internal heat and surface processes.

provenance.source: NASA Earth System Science Framework / AGU

entities.name: Cause of Astronomical Seasons
entities.definition: The cyclical variation in temperature and daylight duration across Earth's year, caused primarily by Earth's 23.5° axial tilt relative to its orbital plane around the Sun, changing solar incidence angle and daylight length.

provenance.source: NASA Science Framework / IAU Astronomy Education

entities.name: Solar System
entities.definition: The gravitationally bound system consisting of the Sun, eight planets and their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids, comets, and interplanetary material, orbiting the Sun.

provenance.source: NASA / IAU

entities.name: Water Cycle
entities.definition: The continuous circulation of water between the atmosphere, Earth's surface, and underground reservoirs through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff, driven by solar energy and gravity.

provenance.source: NOAA / WMO Atmospheric Science Standards

entities.name: Engineering Design Process
entities.definition: An iterative problem-solving methodology involving problem definition, criteria and constraint identification, concept generation, modeling, prototyping, testing, trade-off evaluation, and design optimization.

provenance.source: NGSS Engineering Design Standards / NAE

entities.name: Observation vs. Inference
entities.definition: The epistemic distinction between direct empirical data gathered through sensing/measurement (observation) and the logical explanation or conclusion derived from those data based on prior knowledge (inference).

provenance.source: OECD PISA Epistemic Knowledge Framework / NSTA Nature of Science

entities.name: Algebraic Expression
entities.definition: A combination of variables, numbers, and arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation) that represents a value. Unlike an equation, an expression has no equality sign and cannot be "solved" — it can only be simplified or evaluated.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Angle
entities.definition: The figure formed by two rays (sides) sharing a common endpoint (vertex). Measured in degrees (°) or radians (rad). One full rotation = 360° = 2π rad.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Area
entities.definition: The measure of the size of a two-dimensional surface or region. Measured in square units. The amount of space enclosed within a boundary.
entities.equation: Rectangle: A = l × w  |  Triangle: A = ½ × b × h  |  Circle: A = πr²

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Arithmetic Sequence
entities.definition: A sequence in which each term differs from the previous one by a constant amount called the common difference d, so aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d. The terms grow or decrease linearly, and the sum of the first n terms can be written compactly as Sₙ = n/2 (a₁ + aₙ).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Circle
entities.definition: The set of all points in a plane that are at a fixed distance (radius) from a fixed point (center). Key elements: radius (r), diameter (d = 2r), circumference (C), area (A).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Combination
entities.definition: An unordered selection of items taken from a larger collection, where order does not matter. The number of ways to choose r items from n distinct items is C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n − r)!), often written as a binomial coefficient (n choose r).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Complex Number
entities.definition: A number of the form a + bi, where a and b are real and i is the imaginary unit with i² = −1. The complex numbers extend the real numbers so that every non-constant polynomial has a root, and are represented as points in a plane with a real axis and an imaginary axis.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Continuity
entities.definition: A property of a function at a point when the function value equals its limit there: lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c). A function is continuous on an interval if it is continuous at every point of that interval, meaning its graph can be drawn without lifting the pen. Continuity is a prerequisite for differentiability and for many fundamental results of calculus.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Decimal
entities.definition: A representation of numbers using base-10 place value, where a decimal point separates the whole number part from the fractional part. Each position represents a power of 10.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Derivative
entities.definition: The instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to its variable; the limit of the average rate of change as the interval shrinks to zero. Written f′(x) = lim_{h→0} (f(x+h) − f(x))/h, the derivative gives the slope of the tangent line to the graph at a point.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Determinant
entities.definition: A scalar value computed from a square matrix that encodes geometric and algebraic properties of the matrix, such as whether its linear transformation is invertible. For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] the determinant is ad − bc. A zero determinant means the matrix is singular.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Exponential Function
entities.definition: A function of the form f(x) = a·bˣ where the base b is positive and not equal to 1, with x as the exponent. The function multiplies by a fixed factor b over each unit interval, producing constant relative growth (or decay) rather than constant absolute change.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Fraction
entities.definition: A numerical quantity that is not a whole number, representing a part of a whole. Written as a/b where a is the numerator (number of parts) and b ≠ 0 is the denominator (total equal parts in the whole).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Function
entities.definition: A relation between a set of inputs (domain) and a set of possible outputs (codomain) where each input is related to exactly one output. Written as f: X → Y or y = f(x). The function assigns a unique output f(x) to each input x.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
entities.definition: A theorem connecting differentiation and integration. Part 1 states that the derivative of the integral of f from a to x is exactly f(x); Part 2 states that a definite integral is evaluated by an antiderivative: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a) whenever F′ = f. The theorem makes derivatives and integrals inverse operations.
entities.equation: d/dx ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt = f(x)   and   ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a)

provenance.source: Standard content of calculus curricula; classical theorem (Newton, Leibniz)

entities.name: Geometric Sequence
entities.definition: A sequence in which each term is obtained from the previous one by multiplying by a constant called the common ratio r, so aₙ = a₁·rⁿ⁻¹. The terms change by a constant factor, growing exponentially when |r| > 1 and shrinking toward zero when |r| < 1. The sum of the first n terms is Sₙ = a₁(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r) for r ≠ 1.
entities.equation: aₙ = a₁·rⁿ⁻¹   |   Sₙ = a₁(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r)   (r ≠ 1)

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Integer
entities.definition: The set of whole numbers and their negatives, including zero: ..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ... Integers extend natural numbers to include negative values and zero, enabling subtraction to be closed within the set.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Integral
entities.definition: A quantity that accumulates a function over an interval: the definite integral ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx measures the signed area under the curve y = f(x) between a and b, while the indefinite integral is an antiderivative or a family of functions whose derivative is f. Integration reverses differentiation.
entities.equation: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx  =  F(b) − F(a)  where  F′ = f

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Irrational Number
entities.definition: A real number that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers. Its decimal representation neither terminates nor repeats. Together with rational numbers, they form the real numbers.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Limit
entities.definition: The value a function or sequence approaches as its input or index approaches a given value. Written lim_{x→c} f(x) = L, a limit describes the behaviour of f near the point c without requiring f to be defined there. Limits formalize instantaneous change and underpin the derivative and the integral.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Linear Equation
entities.definition: An equation in which the highest power of the variable is 1. In one variable: ax + b = 0 (a ≠ 0). In two variables: ax + by + c = 0. The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line.
entities.equation: ax + b = 0  (one variable) |  ax + by + c = 0  (two variables)

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Linear Function
entities.definition: A function of the form f(x) = mx + b, where m (slope) and b (y-intercept) are constants. The graph is a straight line. The rate of change (slope) is constant everywhere.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Logarithmic Function
entities.definition: The inverse of the exponential function: y = log_b(x) is the power to which the base b must be raised to obtain x, so bʸ = x. Logarithms convert multiplication into addition and satisfy identities such as log_b(xy) = log_b(x) + log_b(y).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Matrix
entities.definition: A rectangular array of numbers (or other entries) arranged in rows and columns, usually written within brackets. A matrix with m rows and n columns has size m × n. Matrices have defined operations — addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication, and transposition — and provide a compact representation for systems of linear equations and linear transformations.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Mean (Arithmetic Average)
entities.definition: The sum of all values in a data set divided by the number of values. It represents the central tendency or "balance point" of the data.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Median
entities.definition: The middle value in an ordered data set. If there are two middle values, the median is their average. It divides the data into two equal halves and is robust against outliers.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Natural Number
entities.definition: The numbers used for counting and ordering: 1, 2, 3, ... Natural numbers are the most basic number system and form the foundation for all other number systems.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Percentage
entities.definition: A ratio or fraction expressed as parts per hundred, denoted with the % symbol. x% means x/100 or x hundredths. Percentages provide a standardized way to compare proportions regardless of the whole's size.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Permutation
entities.definition: An ordered arrangement of a subset of items drawn from a larger collection, where order matters. The number of ways to arrange r items selected from n distinct items is P(n, r) = n! / (n − r)!; arranging all n items gives n! possibilities.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Polynomial
entities.definition: An algebraic expression consisting of variables and coefficients, involving only the operations of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and non-negative integer exponents. General form: aₙxⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + ... + a₁x + a₀, where n is the degree.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Probability
entities.definition: A measure of the likelihood that an event will occur, expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). P(E) = Number of favorable outcomes / Total number of possible outcomes (for equally likely outcomes).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Proportion
entities.definition: An equation stating that two ratios are equal. If a:b = c:d, then a, b, c, d are in proportion. This means a/b = c/d, or equivalently a×d = b×c (cross-multiplication).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Pythagorean Theorem
entities.definition: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides. This is one of the most fundamental theorems in geometry, connecting algebra and geometry.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Quadratic Equation
entities.definition: An equation in which the highest power of the variable is 2. Standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Quadratic equations have at most two real solutions (roots), found by factoring, completing the square, or the quadratic formula.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Quadratic Function
entities.definition: A function of the form f(x) = ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0). The graph is a parabola. If a > 0, parabola opens upward (minimum at vertex); if a < 0, opens downward (maximum at vertex). The vertex form f(x) = a(x - h)² + k reveals the vertex (h, k).
entities.equation: f(x) = ax² + bx + c  |  f(x) = a(x - h)² + k

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Ratio
entities.definition: A comparison of two quantities by division, expressed as a:b or a/b. Ratios describe the relative size of two quantities without requiring a common unit (unlike percentages which are always per hundred).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Rational Number
entities.definition: Any number that can be expressed as the quotient p/q of two integers, where q ≠ 0. Rational numbers include all integers, fractions, terminating decimals, and repeating decimals.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Sequence
entities.definition: An ordered list of terms a₁, a₂, a₃, … in which a formula or rule assigns a term to each index n (usually a natural number). Sequences are functions whose domain is a set of consecutive integers, and they are classified by their patterns into types such as arithmetic and geometric sequences.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Standard Deviation
entities.definition: A measure of dispersion that quantifies how spread out a data set is around its mean. It is the square root of the variance; for a set x₁, …, xₙ it equals sqrt((1/n) Σ (xᵢ − μ)²) where μ is the mean. A small standard deviation indicates values clustered near the mean, and a large one indicates wide spread.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

entities.name: Triangle
entities.definition: A polygon with three edges and three vertices. The sum of interior angles is always 180°. Triangles are classified by sides (equilateral, isosceles, scalene) and angles (acute, right, obtuse).

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Trigonometric Ratio
entities.definition: Ratios of sides in a right triangle relative to an acute angle. The three primary ratios: sine (opposite/hypotenuse), cosine (adjacent/hypotenuse), tangent (opposite/adjacent). Extended to reciprocal ratios: cosecant, secant, cotangent.
entities.symbol: sin θ, cos θ, tan θ
entities.equation: sin θ = opp/hyp  |  cos θ = adj/hyp  |  tan θ = opp/adj

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Variable
entities.definition: A symbol (usually a letter) that represents an unknown or changeable quantity. Variables allow generalization of arithmetic relationships and the formulation of algebraic expressions and equations.

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Volume
entities.definition: The measure of the three-dimensional space occupied by an object or enclosed by a surface. Measured in cubic units. Capacity refers to how much a container can hold.
entities.unit: cubic metre (m³), cubic centimetre (cm³), litre (L = 1000 cm³)
entities.equation: Cuboid: V = l × w × h  |  Cylinder: V = πr²h  |  Sphere: V = ⁴/₃πr³

provenance.source: NCTM Principles and Standards / ICSE Mathematics Curriculum

entities.name: Acceleration
entities.definition: The rate of change of velocity with respect to time; a vector quantity. Acceleration occurs whenever an object's velocity changes — whether in magnitude, direction, or both.

entities.name: Amplitude
entities.definition: The maximum displacement of a wave from its equilibrium (rest) position. Amplitude determines the energy carried by the wave — greater amplitude means greater energy.

entities.name: Atomic Structure
entities.definition: The structure of an atom as a dense, positively charged nucleus (containing protons and neutrons) surrounded by negatively charged electrons in orbitals. The number of protons determines the element.

entities.name: Bohr Model
entities.definition: Early quantum model of the atom with electrons in quantized circular orbits around nucleus, explaining hydrogen spectrum but limited to hydrogen-like atoms.

provenance.source: Bohr 1913

entities.name: Brownian Motion
entities.definition: Random, erratic motion of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid, caused by collisions with fast-moving molecules of the fluid. Evidence for molecular-kinetic theory.

provenance.source: Einstein 1905; Perrin 1908

entities.name: Buoyancy
entities.definition: The upward force exerted by a fluid on an object immersed in it. This force equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object (Archimedes' principle).

entities.name: Capacitance
entities.definition: The ability of a system of conductors separated by an insulator to store electric charge, measured as the ratio of stored charge to the potential difference across the system. A capacitor is the device realizing this property.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Change of State
entities.definition: The transition of matter between solid, liquid, and gas phases. During a change of state, temperature remains constant as energy is used to break or form intermolecular bonds.

entities.name: Law of Conservation of Energy
entities.definition: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transferred from one object to another or converted from one form to another. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.
entities.equation: E_initial = E_final ; KE_i + PE_i = KE_f + PE_f (conservative systems)

entities.name: Coulomb's Law
entities.definition: The electrostatic force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of their magnitudes and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

entities.name: Electric Current
entities.definition: The flow of electric charge through a conductor. Current is measured as the rate of flow of charge past a point in a circuit.

entities.name: Density
entities.definition: The mass per unit volume of a substance. Density determines whether objects float or sink in fluids.

entities.name: Displacement
entities.definition: The change in position of an object, measured as a straight-line vector from the initial position to the final position. Displacement has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity.

entities.name: Distance
entities.definition: The total length of the path traveled between two positions, regardless of direction. Distance is a scalar quantity — it has magnitude but no direction.

entities.name: Doppler Effect
entities.definition: The apparent change in the observed frequency of a wave due to relative motion between the wave source and the observer. The observed frequency is higher as the source approaches and lower as it recedes.
entities.equation: f_obs = f · (v ± v_o)/(v ∓ v_s) for a wave of speed v

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Efficiency
entities.definition: The ratio of useful energy output to total energy input, expressed as a percentage. No real machine can be 100% efficient because some energy is always dissipated (usually as heat).

entities.name: Electric Charge
entities.definition: A fundamental property of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electromagnetic field. Charge can be positive or negative; like charges repel, opposite charges attract.

entities.name: Electric Field
entities.definition: The region of space surrounding a charge in which another charge experiences a force; quantified as the electric force per unit positive test charge at a point.
entities.equation: E = F/q (definition); E = k·Q/r² for a point charge Q

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Electric Motor
entities.definition: An electrical machine that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy through the interaction between a magnetic field and winding currents producing rotational force (torque).

provenance.source: IEEE / UNESCO Engineering & Physics Education Framework

entities.name: Electromagnetic Induction
entities.definition: The production of an electromotive force (voltage) across a conductor when it is exposed to a changing magnetic field. This is the principle behind electric generators.

entities.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum
entities.definition: The range of all types of electromagnetic radiation, ordered by wavelength or frequency. From longest wavelength to shortest: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.
entities.equation: c = f·λ (applies to all EM waves)

entities.name: Electromagnetic Wave
entities.definition: A transverse self-propagating disturbance of perpendicular electric and magnetic fields that travels through space at the speed of light, requiring no material medium. The electromagnetic spectrum orders such waves by frequency and wavelength.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Electromagnetism
entities.definition: The branch of physics dealing with the relationship between electricity and magnetism. A changing electric field produces a magnetic field, and a changing magnetic field produces an electric field.

entities.name: Energy
entities.definition: The capacity to do work or produce change. Energy exists in many forms and can be transferred between objects or converted from one form to another, but it is never created or destroyed.

entities.name: Energy Loss
entities.definition: The conversion of useful energy into forms that are not available for doing the intended work, typically thermal energy due to friction, air resistance, or other dissipative processes. Energy is conserved overall, but its usefulness decreases.

entities.name: Energy Sources
entities.definition: The origins of energy used by human civilization. Energy sources are classified as renewable (naturally replenished) or non-renewable (finite and depleting).

entities.name: Equations of Motion
entities.definition: The set of kinematic equations relating displacement, initial velocity, uniform acceleration, and time for motion in a straight line under constant acceleration: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as, and s = ½(u + v)t. They apply only when acceleration is constant.
entities.equation: v = u + at;  s = ut + ½at²;  v² = u² + 2as;  s = ½(u+v)t

provenance.source: Nepal CDC SEE / CBSE / UK KS4 kinematics objectives

entities.name: Force
entities.definition: An influence that can change the motion of a body — that is, accelerate it. In classical mechanics the net force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum. Force is a vector quantity.

entities.name: Free Fall
entities.definition: Motion under the influence of gravitational force alone, with no other forces (especially air resistance) acting. In free fall, all objects experience the same acceleration regardless of mass, provided air resistance is negligible.

entities.name: Frequency
entities.definition: The number of complete wave cycles passing a given point per unit time. Frequency determines the pitch of sound and the color of light.

entities.name: Friction
entities.definition: A contact force that opposes the relative motion (or tendency of relative motion) between two surfaces in contact. Friction acts parallel to the contact surface and opposite to the direction of motion or attempted motion.
entities.equation: f = μ·N (for sliding friction; μ = coefficient of friction, N = normal force)

entities.name: Electric Generator
entities.definition: A machine that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction, forcing electric charge to flow through an external circuit by rotating a coil in a magnetic field.

provenance.source: IEEE / IUPAP Physics Education Standards

entities.name: Graphical Analysis of Motion
entities.definition: The use of graphs to represent and analyze motion. Distance-time and velocity-time graphs provide visual tools for understanding motion and extracting quantitative information.

entities.name: Gravitation
entities.definition: The natural phenomenon by which all objects with mass or energy are attracted toward one another. Gravitation is a fundamental interaction that governs the motion of planets, stars, galaxies, and the structure of the universe.

entities.name: Gravitational Acceleration
entities.definition: The acceleration experienced by an object solely under the influence of Earth's gravity, near the Earth's surface. It is approximately constant for all objects, regardless of their mass.

entities.name: Half-Life
entities.definition: The time required for half the nuclei in a radioactive sample to decay. It is a statistically defined constant for a given nuclide and independent of the sample size.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Heat
entities.definition: Energy transferred from one body to another due to a temperature difference. Heat is energy in transit — it is not stored in an object (the stored energy is internal energy).
entities.equation: Q = m·c·ΔT (specific heat) ; Q = m·L (latent heat)

entities.name: Heat Capacity
entities.definition: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of an entire object by one unit of temperature. It depends on the object's size and material, unlike the intensive specific heat which is heat capacity per unit mass.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Heating Effect of Electric Current
entities.definition: The phenomenon by which electrical energy is converted to thermal energy when current flows through a conductor with resistance. The heat produced depends on the current, resistance, and time.

entities.name: Ideal Gas Model
entities.definition: Simplified model of a gas as point particles with no intermolecular forces, obeying PV = nRT. Valid at moderate pressure and high temperature.

provenance.source: Atkins Physical Chemistry

entities.name: Impulse
entities.definition: The product of the average force acting on an object and the time interval over which it acts. Impulse equals the change in momentum of the object.
entities.unit: newton second (N·s) or kilogram metre per second (kg·m/s)

entities.name: Inertia
entities.definition: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion — whether at rest or moving with constant velocity. Inertia is not a force; it is a property of matter quantified by mass.

entities.name: Kinetic Energy
entities.definition: The energy possessed by an object due to its motion. The kinetic energy of an object depends on its mass and the square of its speed.

entities.name: Lens
entities.definition: A transparent optical device that refracts light to converge or diverge rays. Convex (converging) lenses bring light to a focus; concave (diverging) lenses spread light apart.

entities.name: Light
entities.definition: Electromagnetic radiation that is visible to the human eye. Light behaves both as a wave and as a particle (photon); the two models describe complementary aspects of its behaviour.
entities.equation: c = f·λ (c = speed of light in vacuum ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s)

entities.name: Magnetic Field
entities.definition: The region around a magnet or current-carrying conductor where magnetic forces can be detected. Magnetic fields are represented by field lines that show the direction and strength of the field.

entities.name: Magnetic Flux
entities.definition: A measure of the total magnetic field passing through a given surface area, calculated as the product of magnetic field strength perpendicular to the surface and the surface area.

provenance.source: IUPAP Symbols, Units, Nomenclature in Physics

entities.name: Magnetic Force
entities.definition: The force exerted by a magnetic field on a moving charge or on a current-carrying conductor. It is perpendicular to both the velocity of the charge and the magnetic field, so it changes the direction of motion but not the speed of a free charge.
entities.equation: F = q·v×B for a charge q moving at velocity v in field B

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Magnetism
entities.definition: The phenomenon by which materials exert attractive or repulsive forces on other materials. Magnetism is intimately connected to electricity — moving charges produce magnetic fields, and changing magnetic fields produce electric currents.

entities.name: Mass
entities.definition: A property of a body that quantifies its resistance to acceleration in Newtonian mechanics; an intrinsic property independent of location.

entities.name: Measurement
entities.definition: The process of comparing an unknown quantity with a known standard (unit) to obtain a numerical value. Measurement connects physical quantities to mathematics, enabling quantitative description and prediction.

entities.name: Mechanical Advantage
entities.definition: The factor by which a machine multiplies the input force. Mechanical advantage allows a smaller force to produce a larger force, though over a shorter distance.

entities.name: Mirror
entities.definition: A surface that reflects light. Plane mirrors produce virtual images of the same size; curved (concave and convex) mirrors can produce real or virtual images of varying sizes.

entities.name: Momentum
entities.definition: The product of a body's mass and velocity; a vector quantity that is conserved in closed systems. Momentum quantifies the "amount of motion" an object possesses.

entities.name: Motion
entities.definition: The change in position of an object with respect to time and a reference point. Motion is the most fundamental phenomenon studied in mechanics.

entities.name: Newton's First Law of Motion
entities.definition: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion continues in motion with constant velocity (constant speed in a straight line), unless acted upon by a net external force.

entities.name: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
entities.definition: Every mass attracts every other mass with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.

entities.name: Newton's Second Law
entities.definition: The net force acting on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum; at constant mass this reduces to F = m·a.
entities.equation: F = dp/dt (general); F = m·a at constant mass

entities.name: Newton's Third Law of Motion
entities.definition: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. When object A exerts a force on object B, object B simultaneously exerts a force equal in magnitude and opposite in direction on object A.

entities.name: Nuclear Binding Energy
entities.definition: The energy required to separate a nucleus into its individual nucleons, equivalent to the mass defect through the mass-energy relation. It reflects the energy released when a nucleus forms from its constituents.
entities.unit: joule (J) per nucleus; electronvolt (eV) per nucleon
entities.equation: E_b = Δm·c², where Δm is the mass defect

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Nuclear Fission
entities.definition: The splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into smaller nuclei, accompanied by the release of large amounts of energy. Fission is the process used in nuclear power plants.

entities.name: Nuclear Fusion
entities.definition: The combining of light atomic nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, accompanied by the release of large amounts of energy. Fusion is the process that powers the Sun and stars.

entities.name: Ohm's Law
entities.definition: The current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant. The constant of proportionality is the resistance.

entities.name: Our Environment
entities.definition: The study of how physical processes interact with the natural environment, including energy flow, pollution, and the physics of climate and ecosystems.

entities.name: Phase Change
entities.definition: A transition of matter between solid, liquid, and gas states in which the identity of the substance is preserved while its internal structure changes. Latent heat is absorbed or released at constant temperature during such a transition.
entities.unit: joule per kilogram (J/kg) for latent heat

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Photoelectric Effect
entities.definition: Emission of electrons from a material when light of sufficient frequency shines on it, demonstrating quantum nature of light.

provenance.source: Einstein 1905

entities.name: Physical Quantity
entities.definition: A property of a phenomenon, body, or substance that can be quantified — that is, expressed as a number and a reference (unit). Physical quantities describe the physical world in measurable terms, enabling comparison, calculation, and prediction.

entities.name: Potential Energy
entities.definition: The energy stored in an object due to its position, configuration, or condition. Gravitational potential energy depends on mass, gravitational acceleration, and height above a reference level.

entities.name: Power
entities.definition: The rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. Power measures how quickly energy is converted from one form to another.

entities.name: Pressure
entities.definition: The force applied per unit area on a surface. Pressure explains how forces are distributed over areas.

entities.name: Projectile Motion
entities.definition: The motion of an object thrown or launched into the air, moving under the influence of gravity alone (neglecting air resistance). The horizontal and vertical components of motion are independent.
entities.equation: Range = v²·sin(2θ)/g ; Time of flight = 2·v·sin(θ)/g ; Max height = v²·sin²(θ)/(2g)

entities.name: Quantized Energy Levels
entities.definition: The discrete set of energies that a bound system, such as an atom, may possess. Transitions between levels involve the absorption or emission of a photon whose energy equals the difference between the two levels.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Radioactivity
entities.definition: The spontaneous emission of radiation from an unstable atomic nucleus. The three main types are alpha particles, beta particles, and gamma rays.

entities.name: Ray Model of Light
entities.definition: A simplified geometric model of light propagation in which light is represented as straight lines (rays) traveling through transparent media and changing direction at boundaries via reflection or refraction.

provenance.source: IUPAP / UNESCO Physics Education Standards

entities.name: Reflection of Light
entities.definition: The bouncing back of light from a surface. The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

entities.name: Refraction of Light
entities.definition: The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another, caused by a change in light's speed in different media.
entities.equation: n = c/v (refractive index) ; Snell's law: n₁·sin(θ₁) = n₂·sin(θ₂)

entities.name: Electrical Resistance
entities.definition: The opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor. Resistance converts electrical energy to thermal energy.

entities.name: Scalar Quantity
entities.definition: A quantity that has magnitude but no direction. Scalars are fully described by a numerical value and a unit, and follow ordinary arithmetic rules of addition.

entities.name: Simple Harmonic Motion
entities.definition: Motion in which the restoring force on an object is directly proportional to its displacement from equilibrium and opposite in direction, producing a sinusoidal variation of displacement with time.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Sound
entities.definition: A mechanical wave produced by vibrating objects, transmitted through a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) as a longitudinal wave. Sound cannot travel through vacuum.

entities.name: Specific Heat Capacity
entities.definition: The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kilogram of a substance by 1 kelvin (or 1 degree Celsius). Different substances have different specific heat capacities.

entities.name: Speed
entities.definition: The rate at which an object covers distance — the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Speed is a scalar quantity.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.definition: A measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance. Temperature determines the direction of heat flow — heat flows from higher temperature to lower temperature.

entities.name: Thermal Energy
entities.definition: The total internal kinetic and potential energy of the particles in a substance, associated with their random motion and interactions. Thermal energy is related to temperature but distinct from it — it depends on mass, temperature, and the nature of the substance.

entities.name: Time
entities.definition: The dimension that orders events from past through present to future, measured as the interval between two events. Time is a scalar quantity and one of the fundamental base quantities in physics.

entities.name: Unit of Measurement
entities.definition: A standard reference amount of a physical quantity, defined and adopted by convention, against which measurements of that quantity are compared. Units provide the scale that gives physical meaning to numerical values.

entities.name: Vector Quantity
entities.definition: A quantity that has both magnitude and direction, and follows specific rules of addition (vector addition). Vectors represent quantities where direction matters as much as size.

entities.name: Velocity
entities.definition: The rate of change of displacement with respect to time. Velocity is a vector quantity — it has both magnitude (speed) and direction.

entities.name: Potential Difference (Voltage)
entities.definition: The work done per unit charge to move a charge between two points in an electric circuit. Voltage is the "push" that drives current through a circuit.

entities.name: Wave
entities.definition: A disturbance that transfers energy through a medium or through space, without permanently displacing the medium. Waves transfer energy and information from one place to another.

entities.name: Wave Interference
entities.definition: The superposition of two or more waves at a point resulting in a combined disturbance whose amplitude is the sum of the individual amplitudes. Constructive interference occurs when waves are in phase and destructive interference when they are out of phase.
entities.equation: A_result = A1 + A2 (in phase); A_result = |A1 - A2| (oppositely phased)

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics

entities.name: Wave Speed
entities.definition: The speed at which a wave propagates through a medium. Wave speed depends on the properties of the medium, not on frequency or amplitude.

entities.name: Wavelength
entities.definition: The distance between two consecutive points in phase on a wave — for example, crest to crest or trough to trough. Wavelength determines the character of the wave (color of light, pitch of sound).

entities.name: Weight
entities.definition: The gravitational force exerted on an object by a massive body (typically Earth). Weight is a vector quantity acting toward the center of the gravitating body.

entities.name: Work
entities.definition: Energy transferred to or from an object via the application of force along a displacement. For a constant force, work equals the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force: W = F·d·cos(θ). Work is a scalar quantity measured in joules.

provenance.source: Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, 12th Ed.

entities.name: Work-Energy Theorem
entities.definition: The net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy. This theorem connects the concept of work (force × distance) directly to the concept of energy.

entities.name: Scientific Observation
entities.definition: The systematic gathering of information about natural phenomena using the human senses or scientific instruments. Observation provides the empirical basis for scientific questions, hypotheses, and evidence.

provenance.source: OECD PISA 2025 Science Framework / NGSS Science Practices
